survivors: Generating sequences with recurrent neural networks (Graves soft window) 2013
notes: Attention resolved to its two proximate enablers: Graves' 2013 soft window (the differentiable alignment mechanism Bahdanau et al. discuss by name and generalize from monotonic position-based to content-based search) and the bidirectional RNN (1997; RNNsearch's encoder - every annotation the soft search scores is a forward/backward concatenation, paper section 3.1). LSTM rejected as mediated via GRU (the cell actually used); the whole psychology/neuroscience attention canon (Cherry/Broadbent through Itti & Koch) failed directness - name resemblance, no channel. The parent's own template layer was the largest coeval artifact yet: all 16 year-bound drops are 2014, including Cho et al.'s RNN encoder-decoder itself (arXiv June 2014 vs Bahdanau September 2014) plus GRU, seq2seq-as-candidate, Adam, and RAM - at year granularity the architecture attention modified is unrepresentable as its predecessor, the sharpest instance of the coeval artifact so far. Kalchbrenner & Blunsom's recurrent continuous translation models (2013) scouted and failed directness: parallel invention, no consumed channel.

Seq2seq resolved to exactly its two consumed components: the cell (LSTM 1997 - both encoder and decoder are built from it) and the decoder formulation (Mikolov's RNNLM 2010 - the paper defines its decoder as an RNNLM conditioned on the input). The sharpest coeval artifact so far: Cho et al.'s RNN Encoder-Decoder (arXiv June 2014 vs seq2seq September 2014), the single most direct predecessor, dropped at the year bound together with 8 other 2014 artifacts (Devlin NNJM, GRU, Neural Turing Machines, Memory Networks, the WMT'14 dataset itself, dropout, conditional VAE, Chandar et al.) - at year granularity the template seq2seq scaled is unrepresentable as its predecessor. Recipe components behaved as designed: gradient clipping and teacher forcing passed directness (both literally in the paper's training procedure) but failed the Q1/Q2 gate on honest partials - components of a leap, not leaps. Generic substrate rejected as such: backpropagation, BPTT, SGD, CUDA. Two existing nodes (Bidirectional RNNs, Graves soft window) were scouted and matched but rejected for this parent - Sutskever's encoder is a unidirectional LSTM over reversed input, so no false convergence edges; both remain correctly attached at Bahdanau. NPLM rejected as mediated via the RNNLM, its consumed descendant.

BRNN resolved to its single consumed component: the Elman network (1990), the 'regular recurrent neural network' the paper explicitly extends in two directions. One-survivor expansion, like GPT-2's. Coeval artifact: LSTM (1997) dropped at the year bound - BRNN and LSTM are same-year siblings and their famous combination (BLSTM) waited until 2005, so at year granularity the cell BRNN would later marry is unrepresentable at this level. The forward-backward algorithm was graded directness=partial - the two-pass template is structurally identical to HMM smoothing and the authors worked in that tradition, but the paper presents the construction architecturally without citing it; partial fails the gate honestly rather than forcing a verdict. The Elman advance arrived twice in scouting (as 'Elman recurrent network' and as 'Finding structure in time', its own paper title); the second was filed as mediated via the first so the graph keeps exactly one Elman node. TDNN rejected as the overcome prior state (the paper defines itself against the preset future frame); substrate discipline maintained (BPTT/backprop/SGD/Fourier rejected as generic machinery).

parent_name: Generating sequences with recurrent neural networks (Graves soft window)
notes: Graves resolved to its three consumed inputs: the cell (LSTM 1997 - linked, second convergence edge into LSTM after seq2seq), the output formalism (Bishop's MDN 1994, cited as refs [2, 3] in Sec. 4.1), and the corpus (IAM-OnDB 2005, whose own transcriptions define the synthesis conditioning strings in Sec. 5.2). Component discipline held throughout: peephole connections, the forget gate, RMSProp, Graves' elementwise gradient clipping and his adaptive weight noise (variational inference 2011, found consumed in Sec. 4.2 - it produced the paper's best samples) ALL passed directness as literally present in the paper, and ALL failed the Q1/Q2 gate as components of the leap rather than leaps, per the gradient-clipping/teacher-forcing precedent. The RNN transducer (2012) was graded directness=partial: Sec. 5 names it as the model for unknown-alignment prediction, then reports the authors' own transducer experiments 'were not encouraging' and proposes the window as an alternative - the tried-and-replaced prior state, not a consumed component. Sutskever et al. 2011 likewise partial: cited and positioned against, but none of its machinery (multiplicative RNN, Hessian-free training) is consumed. RNNLM was rejected for this parent in explicit contrast to seq2seq, where the paper defines its decoder as a conditional RNNLM (definitional consumption); here it is only the comparison table. BRNN rejected again - the generation networks are strictly unidirectional. CTC mediated via the RNN transducer. Coeval artifacts (4 year-bound drops, all 2013): the sibling ICASSP paper Graves, Mohamed & Hinton 2013 sharing the exact deep-LSTM architecture, Pascanu et al. 2013 formalising the gradient clipping the parent already practised, Hermans & Schrauwen 2013, and word2vec - at year granularity the parent's own twin is unrepresentable as its predecessor.
